rca of the issue: Original prod issue (user-reported): scanner returned 'QR invalide / non reconnu' for new tickets generated by iter-40 make_ticket_image. Two contributing factors confirmed: (1) the iter-40 QR was rendered at ~334px effective size with ECC=H — too dense for some Android camera apps to decode at arm's length. (2) Some scanner apps forward the FULL JSON payload {type:ticket,token,ref} as the path segment, but the backend only knew how to look up by hex32 token or the legacy 10-char printed ref. Iter-41 fix: enlarged the QR to 440px PIL canvas / 395px decoded bbox + dropped ECC to M (still robust, less dense). Added two defensive fallbacks to _resolve_qr_token: step-0 parses a raw JSON payload and extracts obj.token; step-4 prefix-matches booking_id when the input looks like an 8-char hex ref. All 4 input formats now return HTTP 200 on existing bookings. Full check-in walk (aller→retour) persists scans, increments scan_count, flips next_direction, and sets fully_used=true correctly. No code changes required this iteration — the fix is verified and ready for prod. If the user still sees the error after deploy, root cause is browser/service-worker cache on the staff device.
